rules.rule: An identifier followed by parentheses parses as a function call with that name and its arguments in source order; there may be no arguments, and each argument is a full expression, such as a conditional or another call
The last argument may be followed by one comma, but every comma must follow an argument
Arguments must be separated by commas; a newline between two arguments is not a separator
A function call must be closed by a closing parenthesis
An ellipsis after the last argument, optionally separated by whitespace, marks the whole final argument expression for expansion

The ellipsis may only directly follow the last argument inside the parentheses: not an earlier argument, not a lone ellipsis, not before or after a trailing comma and not after the closing parenthesis
Newlines and comments anywhere between the parentheses of a function call are ignored
Spaces and inline comments between the function name and the opening parenthesis are allowed

A newline between the function name and the opening parenthesis is ignored only inside parentheses, tuple brackets, index brackets or function call parentheses; at the top level of an attribute it ends the expression
A function call is an expression term, so attribute accesses, index operations and splats can follow it
Only a plain identifier can be called: attribute accesses, parenthesized expressions, call results and strings can't be followed by an argument list
Identifiers that are keywords only in for expressions, such as for and if, can be called as function names
The identifiers true, false and null followed by parentheses are calls to functions with those names (disputed)
A function name is an identifier, so it can contain dashes and non-ASCII letters

A function name can be several identifiers separated by ::, reported as one name joined with ::, with spaces allowed around :: and newlines only inside parentheses, tuple brackets, index brackets or function call parentheses (disputed)
Each :: in a function name must be preceded by an identifier and followed by an identifier, and a namespaced name must be followed by an argument list
Calling a name that is not in the application's function table is an error when the call is evaluated, not during parsing, so a call that is never evaluated causes no error
Functions and variables are separate namespaces, so a variable does not make a function of the same name callable
A function does not define a variable of the same name, and a function and a variable can share a name and both be used

rules.rule: An argument marked with an ellipsis must evaluate to a list or tuple, otherwise the call is an error
